definitions.explanation: a road or path that has no exit except back the way you came
a situation where no further progress is possible

examples.japanese: この{道|みち}は{行|い}き{止|ど}まりだ。
examples.english: This road is a dead end.

examples.japanese: {行|い}き{止|ど}まりの{標識|ひょうしき}がある。
{間違|まちが}えて{行|い}き{止|ど}まりに{入|はい}ってしまった。
examples.english: I accidentally turned into a dead end.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}は{行|い}き{止|ど}まりに{達|たっ}した。
{研究|けんきゅう}が{行|い}き{止|ど}まりになってしまった。
examples.english: The research has reached a dead end.

examples.japanese: {人生|じんせい}に{行|い}き{止|ど}まりはないと{信|しん}じている。
examples.english: I believe there are no dead ends in life.

notes:
From the verb {行|い}く (to go) + {止|ど}まる (to stop). Used both literally for roads and figuratively for situations with no way forward.

SENSE 1 — PHYSICAL DEAD END:
- {行|い}き{止|ど}まりの{道|みち}: dead end road
- {行|い}き{止|ど}まりの{標識|ひょうしき}: dead end sign

SENSE 2 — FIGURATIVE IMPASSE:
- {行|い}き{止|ど}まりに{達|たっ}する: to reach a dead end/impasse
- {行|い}き{止|ど}まりになる: to hit a dead end
- {交渉|こうしょう}が{行|い}き{止|ど}まり: negotiations are at an impasse

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {突|つ}き{当|あ}たり: end of a road, T-junction (physical only; not used figuratively)
- {袋小路|ふくろこうじ}: cul-de-sac, blind alley (both literal and figurative)
- {膠着状態|こうちゃくじょうたい}: stalemate (figurative only, formal)
